Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

The failing test `testWriteNonAsciiDirectoryNamePosixMode` is attempting to write a non-ASCII directory name to a TAR archive using `TarArchiveOutputStream`. The current bug report mentions an issue when trying to add a directory with a name longer than 100 bytes to the TAR archive, specifically related to writing PAX headers.

Looking at the code of the `putArchiveEntry` method in `TarArchiveOutputStream`, we can see that there is a check for the length of the entry name. If the name length exceeds `TarConstants.NAMELEN` (which is set to 100), different handling mechanisms are triggered based on the `longFileMode`. In the case of `LONGFILE_POSIX` mode, a PAX header with the path is added; in `LONGFILE_GNU` mode, a special GNU long name entry is created.

The failure in the test case and the bug report indicate that the issue may be related to how the `TarArchiveOutputStream` handles long directory names and PAX headers. It seems that when the directory name exceeds 100 bytes, the PAX headers related to it may cause the exception to be thrown due to exceeding the header size.

To address this issue, the `TarArchiveOutputStream.putArchiveEntry` method may need to be modified to handle long directory names and PAX headers more effectively.

Next, I will suggest the best locations to fix this issue.
